sections.h2: Who bills and collects property tax in Onslow County?
sections.html:
The county Tax Office lists and values property, then bills and collects for the county itself and for Holly Ridge, Jacksonville, North Topsail Beach, Richlands and Swansboro. It also takes vehicle tax on the slice of Surf City that sits inside Onslow.

Walk-in service is at 234 NW Corridor Boulevard, Jacksonville, on weekdays between eight and five. The county's published numbers are 910-989-2200 for Administration, 910-989-2201 for Listings, 910-989-2202 for Collections, 910-989-2204 for Land Records and 910-455-7431 for Appraisal. Cash and checks are accepted at the counter. The online tax search and payment site takes cards and e-checks, and it adds a convenience fee.

A seller should phone Collections early. A town bill and a county bill can be separate lines on the same parcel, and Land Records can sort out boundary or owner name questions.

sections.h2: How big is Onslow County and who lives there?
sections.html:
Onslow sits on the coast and covers 762.08 square miles of land. Census QuickFacts puts the 2025 population estimate at 217,175, compared with 204,576 in the 2020 census and 177,772 in 2010. That works out to 268.4 people for each square mile in 2020.

  • Housing stock: 91,470 units, 75,265 households and 63.7 percent owner occupancy for 2020 to 2024.
  • Prices: owners' homes have a middle value of $236,400, and renters pay a middle gross rent of $1,265.
  • Mobility: 78.7 percent of people lived at the same address a year before, so roughly one in five had moved.
  • Veterans: 25,185 live in the county, and 12.8 percent of residents are 65 or over.
  • Building: 1,372 permits were issued in 2025, and the middle household income is $68,148.

A large, mobile population means steady buying and selling, with homes changing hands often enough that payoff and title questions come up every month.

sections.h2: When are Onslow County property taxes due?
sections.html:
Bills go out in July and are due September 1. They count as delinquent when unpaid after January 5 of the next year, according to the county's Taxes Due page. Registered motor vehicle tax rides along with the state's combined vehicle tax and tag system.

State interest rules start the day after that: under G.S. 105-360, 2 percent applies from January 6 to February 1, then 0.75 percent for each month or fraction. The collector reports unpaid real property tax in February, and G.S. 105-369 lets the liens be advertised during March through June.

Bills for 2026 were late. A county notice posted August 18, 2026 said personal property bills would go out the final week of August and real estate notices possibly in early September. The September 1, 2026 due date held, with delinquency after January 5, 2027.

sections.h2: How did the 2026 revaluation change in Onslow County?
sections.html:
Onslow's reappraisal dated January 1, 2026 was postponed a year, so this year's bills rest on the prior reappraisal's values. The county's revaluation page credits Session Law 2026-8 and Session Law 2026-47, and says the new values start in 2027.

A 2001 resolution put Onslow on a four year cycle that began January 1, 2006. State law sets an eight year outer limit and lets a county shorten it.

  • Your 2026 value should mostly match 2025, with changes only for construction or other alterations as of January 1, 2026.
  • Your bill can still rise, since the tax rate set by the Board of Commissioners and by any city or fire district also drives it.
  • An appeal already filed against the 2026 reappraisal value stays alive, and the outcome applies when that value takes effect in 2027.
  • December 31, 2026 was set as the final day to contest the value in use this year, the delayed reappraisal value, or both.

For the 2027 tax year, the usual appeal deadlines and steps return. For the current rate on your parcel, ask the Tax Office or read the rate in the county's adopted budget, since a rate is only final once the Board of Commissioners adopts it.

sections.h2: How do I appeal an Onslow County value?
sections.html:
Begin with an informal review from the Tax Office. If that fails, the formal route runs under the state Machinery Act and differs for real estate, personal property and vehicles, according to the county's Appeals page.

For real estate, ask for the review before formal appeals open in spring. Annual personal property and vehicles need a request inside 30 days of the bill date.

Appeal sequence for an Onslow County parcel
StageTiming
Informal reviewBefore spring formal appeals (real estate); 30 days from the bill date (personal property and vehicles)
Board of equalization and reviewCommissioners serve unless a special board is created; first meeting from the first Monday in April to the first Monday in May
Hearing requestBefore the board adjourns, or 15 days after a late-mailed notice

Sources are the county Appeals page, G.S. 105-322 and G.S. 105-290. The delay changed the 2026 calendar, so confirm dates with the Tax Office.

sections.h2: Which exemptions and relief programs apply?
sections.html:
The county's exemption page mentions exclusion and deferment options, and the state statutes define them. One owner can draw on only one of the three programs below.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion (G.S. 105-277.1): the larger of $25,000 or half the appraised value of a permanent residence. The owner must be 65 or older, or totally and permanently disabled, with income under the limit of $38,800 for 2026.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion (G.S. 105-277.1C): the first $45,000 of value, with no age or income cap.
  • Circuit breaker (G.S. 105-277.1B): tax held to 4 percent of income below the limit, or 5 percent between $38,800 and $58,200, and the excess is deferred as a lien.

Apply on Form AV-9 at the county assessor's office, ideally during January. Applications are accepted through June 1 preceding the tax year, and the circuit breaker needs renewal each year. A sale or transfer ends the deferral, and the prior three years of deferred tax come due, so ask for the full amount before you list.

Active duty service members should read the county's military exemption page. It covers vehicles, boats and mobile homes, and calls for a current Leave and Earnings Statement each year at tag renewal for those claiming another home state.

sections.h2: What happens if I sell with property tax unpaid?
sections.html:
Unpaid tax is a lien on the parcel from the listing date, so it has to be cleared for the buyer to receive clear title. Interest and costs accrue alongside. If the bill sits, the lien can be advertised and foreclosed under G.S. 105-374 or 105-375, and Collections can say which route applies to your parcel.

Selling first keeps the price and timing in your hands. Ask Collections for a payoff listing each taxing unit with a good-through date, since interest steps up on January 6 and again after February 1. Deed tax, at $1 for each $500 of price, is paid by the seller to the register of deeds, and recording fees fall under G.S. 161-10. For a vacant, inherited or run-down house, Cash Home Buyers can make an as-is offer to set beside the payoff and these costs.

faqs.q: What is the due date for Onslow County property tax?
faqs.a: September 1 each year. The county's Taxes Due page says a bill turns delinquent if unpaid after January 5 of the following year, and G.S. 105-360 starts interest on January 6.

faqs.q: Where is the Onslow County Tax Office?
faqs.a: 234 NW Corridor Boulevard in Jacksonville, open weekdays 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Dial 910-989-2202 for Collections or 910-989-2200 for Administration.

faqs.q: Can I still appeal my 2026 Onslow County property value?
faqs.a: The county said appeals could be filed through December 31, 2026, for the value in use this year, the delayed reappraisal value or both. The usual deadlines return for 2027, so call the Tax Office.

faqs.q: Which towns does the Onslow County Tax Office bill for?
faqs.a: The county, plus Holly Ridge, Jacksonville, North Topsail Beach, Richlands and Swansboro. Only vehicle tax is collected for the Onslow portion of Surf City.

faqs.q: Do I owe property tax on a house I am selling?
faqs.a: Yes, until the balance is paid or paid off. Unpaid tax is a lien from the listing date, so a buyer's title search will find it. Ask Collections for a payoff and the closing agent to pay it at closing.
